concepts.name: Devanagari vowels and matras
concepts.summary: Recognise the independent vowels and explain how each attaches to a consonant as a matra sign.

concepts.name: Consonant grid and sounds
concepts.summary: Recall the consonants in their articulation groups and pronounce them, including aspirated and retroflex contrasts.

concepts.name: Inherent a and reading
concepts.summary: Understand that each consonant carries an inherent a and that this is sometimes dropped, so words are read as syllables.

concepts.name: Numbers one to hundred
concepts.summary: Recall the Hindi number words up to 100, which are largely irregular, and the Devanagari numerals.

concepts.name: Pronouns and hona present
concepts.summary: Understand the personal pronouns and form simple present sentences of identity and state with hona.

concepts.name: Basic greetings and courtesies
concepts.summary: Remember and use common greetings, thanks and farewells appropriate to the situation.

concepts.name: Anusvara chandrabindu and nukta
concepts.summary: Understand how nasalisation marks and the nukta dot change the sound of a letter.

misconceptions.text: Devanagari is an alphabet where each letter is a pure consonant or vowel, just like English.
Matras are separate letters written after the consonant in sound order.
Every consonant is always pronounced with its a sound, including at the end of words.

concepts.name: Conjunct consonant formation
concepts.summary: Read and write common conjuncts by combining half forms and stacked letters, including kshа, tra and gya.

concepts.name: Noun gender and number
concepts.summary: Identify masculine and feminine nouns by endings and form their plural and oblique forms.

concepts.name: Adjective agreement
concepts.summary: Make -a ending adjectives agree with the gender and number of the noun they describe.

concepts.name: Possessive postposition ka ki ke
concepts.summary: Choose ka, ki or ke according to the gender and number of the possessed noun.

concepts.name: Postpositions ko se mein par
concepts.summary: Use ko, se, mein and par after nouns to express location, direction, means and recipients.

concepts.name: Three-way honorific levels
concepts.summary: Select tu, tum or aap with the matching verb form according to relationship and setting.

concepts.name: Present habitual with karna
concepts.summary: Form habitual present sentences with karna and other verbs, agreeing with the subject's gender and number.

misconceptions.text: Postpositions come before the noun like English prepositions.
Ka, ki and ke agree with the possessor, like his and her in English.
Gender can be guessed from meaning, so all words for males are masculine and everything else follows English logic.

concepts.name: Past and future tenses
concepts.summary: Form the simple past, past habitual and future tenses with correct agreement.

concepts.name: Oblique case before postpositions
concepts.summary: Apply oblique endings to nouns, adjectives and pronouns before postpositions, such as ladke ko and mujhe.

concepts.name: Ergative ne construction
concepts.summary: Analyse why transitive perfective verbs agree with the object rather than the subject when the subject takes ne.

concepts.name: Progressive and perfect aspects
concepts.summary: Distinguish ongoing actions with rahna from completed ones and use present and past perfect forms.

concepts.name: Compound verbs
concepts.summary: Analyse how verbs such as dena, lena and jana add completion or direction to a main verb.

concepts.name: Dative experiencer constructions
concepts.summary: Explain how feelings, need and possession are expressed with the experiencer in ko or ke paas.

concepts.name: Subordinate clauses with ki and jo
concepts.summary: Build complex sentences using ki, jo-woh and jab-tab, and analyse their word order.

misconceptions.text: With ne, the verb agrees with the subject as in other tenses.
Ne is used with the subject in every past tense sentence.
Mujhe chahiye is a direct translation of I want, so the speaker is the grammatical subject.

concepts.name: Subjunctive and conditional moods
concepts.summary: Distinguish real, hypothetical and counterfactual conditions and select the proper verb forms.

concepts.name: Passive and impersonal forms
concepts.summary: Analyse passive sentences with jana and capability or inability forms such as likha nahin jata.

concepts.name: Register and Hindi-Urdu variation
concepts.summary: Evaluate Sanskrit-derived versus Persian-Arabic vocabulary and judge the register that fits a context.

concepts.name: Colloquial speech and Bollywood idiom
concepts.summary: Interpret informal contractions, slang, code-mixing and dialogue conventions in films and songs.

concepts.name: Causative and derived verbs
concepts.summary: Analyse how verb stems form transitive and causative pairs like banna, banana, banwana.

concepts.name: Discourse particles and emphasis
concepts.summary: Evaluate the effect of particles hi, bhi, to and word order on emphasis and tone.

concepts.name: Idioms and proverbs
concepts.summary: Interpret common muhavare and proverbs and choose them appropriately in speech.

misconceptions.text: Hindi and Urdu differ only in script, so register differences do not matter.
Filmi Hindi is a reliable model for everyday polite speech.
Particles like hi and bhi are filler that does not change meaning.

concepts.name: Stylistic choice across genres
concepts.summary: Evaluate how diction, syntax and register differ across news, poetry, film and conversation and justify choices.

concepts.name: Literary and poetic forms
concepts.summary: Assess meter, imagery and traditional forms such as doha and ghazal in Hindi literature.

concepts.name: Translation and cultural adaptation
concepts.summary: Produce translations that preserve tone, honorific level and cultural reference rather than literal wording.

concepts.name: Dialect and language contact
concepts.summary: Evaluate how Awadhi, Braj, Bhojpuri and English shape standard Hindi, and judge code-switching norms.

concepts.name: Original writing and speech
concepts.summary: Compose original essays, dialogues or scripts with register control, idiom and natural rhythm.

concepts.name: Orthographic and normative issues
concepts.summary: Judge disputes over spelling, nukta use, anusvara versus nasal consonant and loanword adoption using normative sources.

misconceptions.text: Standard Hindi is a single uniform language and dialects are just incorrect speech.
A good translation maps each Hindi word to one English word.
Using English words in Hindi always signals poor command of the language.
